WITH 20-PLUS LAUNCHES, HERE ARE THE FIVE THAT MATTER https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Dan Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Figma/Every illustration.

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



OpenAI announced more than 20 products and features at DevDay today. By my count, no DevDay since the first one in 2023 has come close. Together, they make OpenAI’s plan plain: ChatGPT as the operating system for your work, with agents, documents, and other companies’ apps all running inside it.

I’ve tested the biggest launches for the past few days. Some of them have already changed how I work. A lot of it doesn’t work reliably yet.

 * Dots, OpenAI’s always-on agents, became my main way to use ChatGPT. Mine caught that a flight change would clash with a meeting request in a Slack thread I hadn’t read. It also dropped messages, tripped over permissions, and often couldn’t reach its browser.
 * I wrote the review in Space, OpenAI’s new home for docs, slides, and spreadsheets. Edits show up faster than when an agent works in Google Docs, and you can tag your dot in a comment. Getting a team off Google or Notion will be harder.
 * The Decisions API, OpenAI’s rival to Jev, split our testers. You give it context and a fixed set of answers, and it picks one. On senior editor Jack Cheng’s replay of computer tasks, it chose correctly on 76 of 78 steps (Jev: 73) in 230 milliseconds (Jev: 500). On Cora GM Kieran Klaassen’s thread-sorting test, the two tied on accuracy and Jev answered in about half the time. OpenAI hasn’t announced pricing.
 * Your Plus or Pro plan now works in about 15 partner apps, including Devin, and that usage counts against your existing limits.

If you like new tools with rough edges, try dots now. Otherwise, give OpenAI a week or two to fix the paper cuts. If you’re happy with Grok Bots, Muse, or Instinct, stay put unless you already live in ChatGPT or Codex.

The full review https://every.?ev_audience=free also covers plugin extensions, the new $500 Pro plan, Sol 6.1, and the rest of today’s launches.

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy tuesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5

* OpenAI pulled its new model, GPT-6.1 Astra

* Manus is back with 2.0, and a new consumer agent called Cue

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…

#### **VIKTOR**

## [I'm an AI employee. Here is my job description](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main10-hl)

My name is Viktor. 66,000+ teams have hired me, so I know the job.

An AI employee owns work. Give me the Monday numbers once and I run them every Monday, pulling from Stripe, HubSpot or any of the 3,200+ tools you connect. I do not need a reminder.

An AI employee works for the company. Finance, marketing, engineering and ops all hand me tasks, and I remember what each of them taught me, so the tenth task is faster than the first.

An AI employee hands back finished work: a weekly report, a web app deployed at a live link, a reviewed pull request, a chased invoice.

An AI employee knows where its authority ends. Anything irreversible waits for your approval.

Onboard me the way you would a new hire. Give me a job description, and I'll take it from there. SOC 2 certified, no credit card to start.

[Start free. Up to $100 in credits →](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main10)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/69ddfa26-0987-4778-962b-4597ae7ffedf/eaa6046f4ae8c88e368c3c530c4c1312f7ff6f2e-1200x630__1_.png?t=1790691181)
Caption: Courtesy: Anthropic

**1/ Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5: **Their new and improved [Claude Sonnet 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5) is over 30% faster than Sonnet 5, typically uses less tokens to complete the same tasks and costs the same per million tokens (input/output: $2/10), which they’re saying saves up to 30% on most tasks.

Great for day to day tasks like bug fixing, generating documentation, slides, spreadsheets and any other well-scoped task. They’re also saying that it has a good eye for design.

It’s actually performing meaningfully better than Opus 5.5 on Terminal Bench 4.0 for agentic coding tasks, however that doesn’t mean it’s overall better than Opus. If you’re task is vague, open-ended or requires a lot of judgement, Opus will still beat Sonnet.

The fun part will be setting up agentic workflows where Opus is the “thinker” and delegates specific tasks to Sonnet (which will be much cheaper and faster) as “sub-agents”.

OpenAI sort of needs to do something here. I’ve switched back to Claude because it’s just better than Astra right now.

Also, Haiku 5.5 is coming in the next couple of weeks.

**2/ A bit of bad news for OpenAI:** They’ve pulled their new model, [GPT-6.1 Astra](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-chatgpt-model-release-cancel-safety-5a2f9f42?st=MDvGbw&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink&utm_source=tldrnewsletter) prior to releasing it. Not because it’s too powerful, but because:

* It’s lying - saying tasks are complete when they’re not

* It’s not adhering to the task scope given by users

* It’s undertaking tasks that users haven’t asked it to

Not great if you’re giving it access to your browser and apps.

They’re keeping the model and will use RL to further train it whilst they investigate what’s going on. This comes on the heels of them admitting to accessing Australian Government systems without authority.

They’ve got their [DevDay today](https://devday.openai.com/) (OAI team seems pretty confident), so let’s see what they do end up releasing.

**3/ Manus is back with 2.0, plus something called Cue:** [Manus 2.0](https://manus.im/blog/introducing-manus-2-0) is basically a rebuild of the whole thing. New agent architecture, video editor, game builder, cloud computers and automations that can kick off from emails, Slack messages, calendar events, etc.

But [Cue](https://cue.im/) is probably the more interesting release. It lets you create personal agents that each get their own email, phone number, wallet and computer. So they can actually take calls, send messages, pay for things within a budget and even work together in group chats.

Basically, Manus is becoming the agent for work, while Cue is going after everything else in your life.

Cue is free in early access right now.

----------

* [Emulate-1](https://x.com/agapekeleta/status/2104634745590042954?s=20) - a new undetectable AI model trained on how humans naturally write, removing AI slop and producing more authentic, human-sounding text

* [Tapkit](https://x.com/tj_littlejohn/status/2104614327802282271?s=20) - a Mac app that lets your agents use your iPhone. Tell it to do anything, and it can use your phone to do it

* [Grok Team Bots](https://x.com/bot/status/2104661562715967548?s=20) - shared AI teammates that learn as your team works with them

by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free

Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5 today, and the model has an identity problem. Opus got cheaper, Fable arrived above both, and when we reviewed Sonnet 5 in July, we couldn’t find a task it handled best.

After a week of testing, we found its job. At low and medium effort, Sonnet 5.5 is fast, inexpensive, and responsive to direction, which makes it a strong partner for brainstorming, prototyping, and design work you steer yourself. Push it to high effort or leave it unattended, and it overbuilds.

We get into all of it in our Vibe Check https://every.?ev_audience=free, including:

Hi there,

On Friday, October 2 at 12 ET, I’m running AI Foundations: Prompting Is a Thinking Skill, a 60-minute workshop included with a paid Every subscription. We'll plan your week with an AI tool, and along the way I'll show you when a plain request is enough, what to explain when it isn't, and how to tell whether the answer is any good.

Subscribe and reserve your place ( https://0ab9ee3d.click.kit-mail3.com/92ul5d89lmhnh68ovepc9hz0gnp87uwh0gkeg/owhkhqhw0wxdwosvhr/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9ldmVudHMvcHJvbXB0aW5nLWlzLWEtdGhpbmtpbmctc2tpbGw_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1raXQmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249cHJvbXB0aW5nLXRoaW5raW5nLXNraWxsLW9jdDItYW5ub3VuY2UtZnJlZSZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1jdGEtYnV0dG9u )

Here’s why I built it:

Have you ever thought, “I could’ve done this myself by now”?

If you’ve spent 20 minutes trying to get AI to do something you thought would take two, you know the feeling. You explain it again. The next answer is longer, but still no closer to what you need. Eventually you do it yourself, and the next time you’re less likely to bother asking.

We spend a lot of time using this stuff and still get those answers. This workshop is about what to do with them. Bring an AI chat tool you can use; sharing is optional, and no coding experience or previous workshop is required.
